html:
The Yidinji are an Aboriginal Australian people of the rainforest and coast around today's Cairns in north Queensland, from the Mulgrave and Russell rivers up onto the Atherton Tableland. The map shows them in 1783 and 1800.

Like their neighbours the Dyirbal, they lived in rainforest and made toxic nuts edible by careful processing. Their language, Yidiny, was described in a full grammar by the linguist R. M. W. Dixon in 1977. Some Yidinji stories tell of a time when the coastline lay far out to sea, which some scholars read as a memory of the rise in sea level after the last Ice Age. Cairns was founded in 1876, and sugar cane and timber took over the coastal plains. Other neighbours on the map include the Djabugay and the Mbabaram. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
